2.caption: Every sync tool routes it through here.

3.headline: Sync to storage you already own.

narration.1: Every sync tool asks you to trust a server.
narration.2: Your bookmarks, your tabs, your history, all of it through a company's machines, and you take their word for what happens there.
narration.3: Konode syncs the same things. It just doesn't route them through anyone.
narration.4: Add a bookmark on one browser, and it's on the other. Not because we copied it, because your own Drive did.
narration.5: You pick where it lands. Your Google Drive, a private GitHub repository, or any WebDAV server.
narration.6: Bookmarks, open tabs, history, and which extensions are missing on the machine you're sitting at.
narration.7: No account to create. No Konode server to trust. End-to-end encryption if you want it.
